chunks: Does he think his wealth will abide for ever with him?

key_terms.أَخْلَدَهُ: He will make him abide/immortalize him

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the illusion of wealth providing eternal security?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Muddaththir is often linked to the specific context of Abu Jahl, illustrating how the arrogance of the wealthy leads to a delusion of permanence. It serves as a profound critique of materialism, reminding believers that worldly accumulation is transient and cannot secure immortality or divine protection against the Hereafter.
